analysis: Market is in a mixed macro environment — many S&P names still well below 52-week highs after the recent correction, creating Stage 1-to-2 basing opportunities in quality businesses. The portfolio starts fresh (all cash) so we can be selective. Three high-conviction setups stand out: (1) ROP is only 16% off its 52-week low, quietly basing with SMA50 slope turning positive — a deeply discounted quality compounder. (2) V is a near-perfect capital-light business basing in the lower third of its range, near flat vs SMA200 — the trend has stopped going down and valuation is fair. (3) MSFT offers unmatched FCF and AI optionality at a forward P/E of 21 while basing at 30% of its 52-week range. All three have clear fundamental anchors and technical basing signals. Each position is sized at ~25% equity so worst-case simultaneous stop-outs cost ~4% of total equity. Remaining ~25% cash provides dry powder for new entries or adding to winners. Strategy targets 15-20%+ gains over 3-6 months per position, consistent with ~1% weekly compounding goal when winners are held and losers are cut quickly.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $356.56 or better; will also accept a minor pullback to $350-355 near SMA50 as an improved entry. Do not chase above $365.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Roper is a high-quality serial acquirer of niche B2B software and industrial tech businesses with a 27% operating margin, $2.2B FCF, and accelerating 11% revenue growth. Forward P/E of 14.9x is historically cheap for this compounder — priced as if growth is over, which the fundamentals contradict. TECHNICAL: At only 16% of its 52-week range (the lowest of all top candidates), the stock has stopped making new lows. SMA50 slope has turned positive (+0.9% over 20 days) and price sits just +0.7% above SMA50 — a tightly coiled basing pattern consistent with Stage 1-to-2 transition. Risk/reward is asymmetric: 21% upside to $430 (still well below prior highs) vs 5.2% stop.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below $338 stop on volume; (2) SMA50 slope turns sharply negative again over 2+ weeks; (3) any quarter shows FCF deterioration or margin compression without clear one-time explanation; (4) if stock reaches $430 target reassess — if thesis intact and under 1 year, hold for LTCG threshold.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $322 or on any intraday pullback toward $318-322. Avoid chasing if it gaps significantly above $328.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Visa is the highest-conviction quality business in the candidate list — 67% operating margin, 60% ROE, $20.8B FCF, 17% revenue growth, minimal capital requirements, and a near-monopoly on global payment rails. Forward P/E of 21.7x is reasonable for this earnings quality. The business is structurally insulated from tariff/macro noise as it earns on transaction volume rather than goods. TECHNICAL: At 35% of its 52-week range with price nearly flat vs SMA200 (-2.9%) and SMA50 slope slightly negative, the stock is consolidating rather than collapsing. Price is +3.5% above SMA50 — not extended, just recovering. A break higher resumes the long-term uptrend. Stop at 2x ATR yields a tight 4.8% risk with 16.5% upside to $375.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) daily close below $306.57; (2) regulatory action materially impairs Visa's network economics or interchange model; (3) revenue growth decelerates below 10% for two consecutive quarters; (4) target $375 reached — reassess for continuation or partial trim.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $411.38 or pullback toward $405-410. Will use a scale-in approach — initial full position at current levels given clean basing pattern.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Microsoft is one of the highest-quality businesses ever screened — 46% operating margins, $37B FCF (and $170B operating CF), 18.3% revenue growth, and conservative 30x D/E leverage. At a forward P/E of 21.2x and PEG of 1.29 it is meaningfully cheaper than its 3-year average. Azure and Copilot AI monetization are still early-stage revenue tailwinds. The business does not depend on tariff outcomes. TECHNICAL: At 30% of 52-week range ($356-$539) and -11.7% below SMA200, Microsoft is in a basing consolidation phase. SMA50 is still slightly declining (-0.7%/20d) which is why we're not yet confirmed Stage 2, but price just crossed the SMA50 from below (+3.6% above). Stop at 2x ATR ($388) gives 5.6% downside with 16.7% upside to $480, just shy of the prior rejection zone.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) close below $388.34 stop; (2) Azure growth decelerates sharply (below 25% QoQ) or AI monetization thesis reverses; (3) SMA50 slope fails to turn positive within 4-6 weeks; (4) at $480 target evaluate LTCG extension — if within 9 months of 1-year holding threshold, strongly prefer holding through for tax efficiency.
